Reviewer(s)' Comments to Author:

Reviewer: 1

Comments to the Author
This methodological note presents a cogent and well-structured discussion of an LLM-based data extraction method for social scientists. 
The revisions in this second round have immensely improved the clarity of the study and thus highlighted the contribution of it, which I believe will make it highly accessible and useful to many researchers in the field. 
The abstract sets the scene effectively and the overall aim of the paper is now clear from the outset. 
Most of my previous concerns have been comprehensively addressed or further discussed, leaving only minor comments for further consideration.

Introduction

The introduction has been substantially improved, particularly in terms of clarifying the research gap and the intended contribution. 
This makes it much clearer how this methodological note will benefit researchers, especially those less familiar with LLM applications. 
The framing is now much stronger and sets the stage well for the discussion that follows.

Generating the Dataset

One small point I would like to see addressed is a brief but explicit acknowledgement that GPT-based models can make mistakes - something that should be clear to all researchers, and I am sure is clear to you. 
However, I would consider this particularly relevant in the context of the examples given on page 6. 
While I understand that this does not invalidate the approach, it would be beneficial to highlight this limitation, particularly as the authors propose this as a potential method for researchers who may not have technical expertise. 
Making this explicit could help to set appropriate expectations and encourage researchers to use the method critically.

While I agree that validation of this standardised approach is not the primary aim of this note, and the removal of the substantive findings from the example alleviates some concerns, the inclusion of phrases such as "to the best of their knowledge" remains an area that could use more discussion. 
What do researchers gain by extracting responses that would otherwise be rejected due to limited information? This is a validation challenge, and if the authors propose to include such phrases, they should highlight the implications so that researchers can make informed decisions.

Managing the Output

The authors have done a good job of addressing concerns about error and bias within the scope of the study. 
However, I suggest adding a brief discussion of the potential for systematic bias due to missing values. 
While an analysis of bias may be beyond the scope of this paper, it would be valuable to acknowledge that missing values may introduce systematic error. 
As the proposed method specifically allows researchers to identify and manage such biases, it would be helpful to emphasise this point explicitly.

Discussion

The discussion effectively ties back to the introduction and clearly reinforces the study's key messages. This section is well-structured and compelling.

One aspect that could be strengthened is the emphasis on reproducibility and transparency. 
A short note on which aspects of the data generation process should be published to ensure transparency would be useful. 
In addition, recent literature (e.g. Barrie, Palmer & Spirling: "Replication for Language Models: Problems, Principles, and Best Practices for Political Science") highlights the current challenges of replicating studies involving LLMs. 
While the authors do not claim that their method is foolproof, a brief reminder of the importance of standardisation in assessing variability would enrich the discussion. 
Given that the introduction already highlights how standardisation facilitates assessment, revisiting this point in the discussion would strengthen the study's contribution to transparency in LLM-based research.

Conclusion

Overall, this methodological note presents a well-thought-out approach to LLM-based data extraction for social scientists. 
The improvements made in this revision have greatly enhanced its clarity and usefulness. 
The discussion is well-structured, and the proposed method, along with the provided R package, will undoubtedly be valuable to many researchers. 
With the minor adjustments suggested above, the paper will further strengthen its contribution to the field and I am looking forward to seeing it published. 

Reviewer: 2

Comments to the Author

Thank you for your re-submission. 
My comments to the first version were limited as I considered this a small methodological note, and what I read there was sufficient as a first step toward some more ambitious work. 
That was my understanding of the submission.

I can see (also as per the editor comments) that reviewer 1 saw this as a full paper, and then several changes were requested in particular about clarifying aspects relating to models, bias, and the procedure. 
I did not see the issue of e.g. bias as that relevant, mostly because every time we publish on using LLMs we are forced to comment on bias and hallucinations, and this becomes trite and should be rather devoted to tailored/specific papers on i.e. LLMs bias more than on other substantive or methodological work.

Anyway, the changes that I saw do appear well thought, and they certainly add some clarity, even though, to an extent they make the submission much heavier to read, than a leaner methodological note, which I liked in the first place. 

To an extent I understand now the refocusing of the material too, as per the comments received from reviewer 1. 
Albeit I do not contend the choice of the refocus, I think the problem of VAAs was almost more intriguing. 
I can see people going on e.g. chatGPT and ask recommendations for voting, and exploring this as a political science problem seemed to me perhaps the most compelling idea. 
So now the focus is not so much about how people will get voting advice, but rather about what is inside LLMs about politics and to extract it as data.

Given the refocus I am only asking for you to make footnote 2 part of the text. 
I think that is a crucial piece of information (ie the availability of the script for others) now for the new focus.
